svg.font-family: Segoe UI, system-ui, -apple-system, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Halden Distribution P3 privileged access and assessment loop
svg.desc: A three-tier privileged access model for a fictional 85-user company: Tier 0 domain controllers and the privileged access workstation, Tier 1 member servers, Tier 2 workstations and helpdesk, with separate admin accounts in the _Admin OU, and the assessment, remediation and detection loop that runs repeatedly. All activity is confined to an isolated home lab.
svg.text: Halden Distribution Ltd — P3 privileged access and assessment loop
Isolated home lab · domain ad.halden.internal · lab-only assessment with free tools (PingCastle, Purple Knight, BloodHound CE, Windows LAPS)
Tier 0 — domain and identity
DCs · AD · Entra Connect (P2) · PKI · DC backups
DC01 / DC02
WS02 — PAW
Tier 0 logons only (P6 isolates it)
adm-t0-* accounts · G_Tier0_Admins
Protected Users · not delegable · FGPP (20 chars, lockout 5)
Deny logon to Tier 1 servers and every workstation
Tier 1 — member servers
FS01 (files) · LNX01 (app) · CA01 (P6)
FS01 · LNX01 · CA01
adm-t1-* accounts · G_Tier1_Admins
Read LAPS passwords for servers only
Deny logon to DCs and workstations
Tier 2 — workstations and support
WS01 · WS02 (user side) · helpdesk work on user objects
WS01 — Windows 11 Enterprise
unique LAPS password, rotated every 30 days
adm-t2-* accounts · G_Tier2_Helpdesk
Reset password + unlock by delegation on user OUs only
Deny logon to DCs and member servers
Where admin accounts live: the _Admin OU

g.text: _Admin\PAW\Devices → WS02, the Tier 0 privileged access workstation
Every IT person keeps a separate daily-use account with no admin rights.

svg.text: The loop: assess → remediate → detect → verify

g.text: 1. Assess — PingCastle healthcheck, Purple Knight, BloodHound CE
2. Remediate — tiering, Windows LAPS, gMSA, legacy-protocol hardening
3. Detect — NTLM audit events (8004), Kerberos RC4 tickets (4769), LAPS backup (10018)
4. Verify — re-run the tools and the verification script; every finding gets a source
5. Review — monthly privileged-access review; residual risk gets an owner and a date

svg.text: Legend and honest scope

g.text: Halden Distribution Ltd. is a fictional company; the domain, hosts and accounts are the owner's isolated lab.
Weaknesses were seeded deliberately so the assessment has something to find; this is an authorised lab exercise.

svg.text: Footnotes

g.text: No score, path count or coverage figure is shown on this diagram: none has been measured yet.
Every published number will come from a real run in the lab, cited to a file in evidence/public/.

svg.text: Assessment tooling is free and open (PingCastle basic, Purple Knight, BloodHound Community Edition, Windows LAPS). It is run only against the lab domain, with the owner's written authorisation, and the raw output stays out of the published repository.
Diagram is descriptive, not a measurement. Controls are shown as designed; verification results are added to the project README after the lab run.
